parts.problem_md:
This question is about reversible reactions and equilibria.

Give two characteristics of a dynamic equilibrium.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Two characteristics of a dynamic equilibrium are:
> 
> - The forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate
> **OR**
> The rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction **[1 mark]**
> - The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Two key words to remember for this definition are **"rate"** and **"constant"**.
> 
> - The **rates** of the forward and reverse reactions are **equal**.
> - The **concentrations** of all substances are **constant**.
> 
> A common mistake is to say the concentrations are *equal*, which is incorrect. They are just no longer changing.

parts.problem_md:
Ethanol and ethanoic acid react together in a dynamic equilibrium.

The reaction is exothermic.

The equation for the reaction is:

C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (aq) + CH<sub>3</sub>COOH (aq) $\rightleftharpoons$ CH<sub>3</sub>COOC<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

i) Give the name of the organic product

[1]

ii) Predict the effect on the yield of increasing the reaction temperature. Give a reason for your answer.

[2]

iii) The reaction is catalysed by concentrated sulfuric acid. Predict the effect of the catalyst on the reaction yield at equilibrium.

[1]
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> i) The name of the organic product is:
> 
> - Ethyl ethanoate** [1 mark]**
> 
> ii) The effect of increasing the temperature on the yield is:
> 
> - (The yield) decreases** [1 mark]**
> - An increase in temperature shifts the position of equilibrium in the direction of the endothermic reaction **[1 mark]**
> 
> iii) The effect of the catalyst on the reaction yield at equilibrium is:
> 
> - There is no change in yield as a catalyst does not affect the position of equilibrium in a reversible reaction **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> i) Esters are named according to the alcohol and carboxylic acid used. The naming pattern is **alkyl alkanoate**:
> 
> - The alkyl comes from the alcohol
> 
>   - In this case, **eth**anol, so the group is **ethyl**.
> - The alkanoate comes from the carboxylic acid
> 
>   - In this case **ethan**oic, so the group is **ethan**oate.
> 
> ii) The question tells us that the reaction is exothermic, so the reverse reaction is endothermic.
> 
> - Decreasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the exothermic direction.
> - Increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic direction.
> 
> So, a shift to the endothermic direction (left in this case) causes a decrease in the yield of products.
> 
> iii) A catalyst has **no effect** on the yield at equilibrium. It only affects the **rate** of reaction, speeding up both the forward and reverse reactions by the same amount.

parts.problem_md:
Draw an enthalpy level diagram for the reaction between ethanol and ethanoic acid.

Label the enthalpy change, $\Delta$*H*

![Vertical arrow labelled "Energy" pointing upwards on a plain white background, indicating increasing energy along the direction of the arrow.](assets/001-vertical-arrow-labelled-energy-pointing-upwards-.png)
parts.solution_md:
The enthalpy level diagram for the reaction is:

![Energy level diagram showing ethanol and ethanoic acid reacting to form ethyl ethanoate and water, with energy change ΔH marked.](assets/002-energy-level-diagram-showing-ethanol-and-ethanoi.png)

**[3 marks]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> 1 mark for products level lower than reactants level
> 
> 1 mark for the labelled reactants (ethanol + ethanoic acid) **AND  **labelled products (ethyl ethanoate + water)
> 
> 1 mark for the enthalpy change (Δ*H*) shown with a downward pointing arrow from the reactants' level to the products' level

> **[exam-tip]**
> For an **exothermic** reaction, energy is released, so the products have less energy than the reactants. This means the product line must be **lower** than the reactant line.
> 
> The arrow for Δ*H* must start at the reactants' level and point down to the products' level to show that the overall energy change is negative.

parts.problem_md:
The gasification of carbon is a reversible endothermic reaction:

C (s) + H<sub>2</sub>O (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ CO (g) + H<sub>2</sub> (g)

Which of the following conditions could be changed to increase the relative amount of H<sub>2</sub> gas produced?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Increasing the temperature will increase the relative amount of products at equilibrium for an endothermic reaction
- **A** is incorrect as the surface area to volume ratio does not affect the equilibrium position, only the rate
- **B** is incorrect as increasing the pressure will cause the equilibrium position to shift towards the side with the smaller number of molecules of gas, which is the reactant side, decreasing the product
- **D** is incorrect as catalysts do not affect the equilibrium position, only the rate

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: Increase the surface area to volume ratio of the carbon

parts.problem_md:
When hydrogen gas is heated with iodine gas, hydrogen iodide gas is produced.

The equation for this reversible reaction is:

hydrogen  +  iodine  ⇌  hydrogen iodide

This reversible reaction reaches equilibrium in a sealed container.

Place ticks in boxes by the two statements that are correct for when the reaction reaches equilibrium

| The forward reaction and reverse reaction are both exothermic |   |
|---|---|
| The mass of each substance does not change |   |
| The hydrogen no longer reacts with iodine |   |
| The rates of the forward reaction and reverse reaction are equal |   |
| The gases have escaped from the container |   |
parts.solution_md:
The two correct statements are:

| The forward reaction and reverse reaction are both exothermic |   |
|---|---|
| The mass of each substance does not change | ✔ ;** [1 mark]** |
| The hydrogen no longer reacts with iodine. |   |
| The rates of the forward reaction and reverse reaction are equal | ✔; ** [1 mark]** |
| The gases have escaped from the container. |   |

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.problem_md: The forward reaction is exothermic.  Name the type of energy change in the reverse reaction.
parts.solution_md:
The type of energy change in the reverse reaction is:

- Endothermic; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *For a reversible reaction, it is always exothermic in one direction, and endothermic in another*

parts.problem_md:
Hydrogen iodide is colourless.

The colour of hydrogen and iodine in the initial mixture is purple.

When equilibrium is reached, how will the colour of the mixture have changed?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- The mixture would be purple when there is more hydrogen and iodine being produced and the rate of the reverse reaction is greater
- The mixture would be colourless if there is more hydrogen iodide being produced and the rate of the forward reaction is greater
- If the rate at which the reactants and products is made is equal (dynamic equilibrium) it will be somewhere in between purple and colourless so pale purple is the correct option

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: The mixture will have become a paler purple

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The mixture will have become a deeper purple

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The mixture will have become colourless

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: The colour of the mixture will remain unchanged

parts.problem_md:
Changes to the reaction conditions will move the position of the equilibrium.

State two of these reaction conditions.
parts.solution_md:
Two reaction conditions that can be changed to move the position of the equilibrium are:

- Pressure; **[1 mark]**
- Temperature; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *You cannot say concentration as a condition as this question is referring to gases *

parts.problem_md:
The industrial production of sulfuric acid involves several steps.

One of these steps is the reaction of sulfur dioxide, SO<sub>2</sub>, with oxygen to form sulfur trioxide, SO<sub>3</sub>.

2SO<sub>2</sub> (g) + O<sub>2</sub> (g) $\rightleftharpoons$2SO<sub>3</sub> (g)

What volume of sulfur trioxide, in dm<sup>3</sup>, is produced by the complete reaction of 750 dm<sup>3</sup> of sulfur dioxide? (all volumes of gases are measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- One mole of any gas occupies the same volume, 24 dm<sup>3</sup> at room temperature and pressure
- The balanced symbol equation shows for every 2 moles of SO<sub>2</sub>, 2 moles of SO<sub>3</sub> are produced (if it goes to completion)
- As the number of moles are the same, the volume of SO<sub>3</sub> produced from 750 cm<sup>3</sup> of SO<sub>2</sub> will be the same
- A is not correct because 375.5 dm<sup>3</sup> is half the actual volume formed
- C is not correct because 1125.5 dm<sup>3 </sup>is one and a half times the actual volume formed
- D is not correct because 1500 dm<sup>3</sup> is double the actual volume formed

parts.problem_md:
Calculate the volume of oxygen needed to react completely with 750 dm<sup>3</sup> of sulfur dioxide. (all volumes of gases are measured under the same conditions of temperature and pressure)

volume of oxygen = .............................. dm<sup>3</sup>
parts.solution_md:
The volume of oxygen needed to react completely with 750 dm<sup>3</sup> of sulfur dioxide is:

- 1⁄2 x 750 
**OR **
375 (dm<sup>3</sup>);** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *2 moles of SO*<sub>*2*</sub>* will react completely with 1 mole of O*<sub>*2*</sub>*, so the volume of oxygen that will react will be half the volume of SO*<sub>*2*</sub>

The mass, in kilograms, of 750 dm<sup>3</sup> of sulfur dioxide, measured at room temperature and pressure is:

- Moles of SO<sub>2</sub> = $\frac{750}{24}$ (= 31.25); **[1 mark]**
- Mass of SO<sub>2</sub> = $\frac{750}{24}$ x 64 **OR** 31.25 x 64 (= 2000); **[1 mark]**
- Mass of SO<sub>2</sub> = $\frac{2000}{1000}$ (= 2 (kg)); **[1 mark]** 
*Final answer of 2 (kg) with or without working scores 3 marks*

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *The amount, in moles, of SO*<sub>*2*</sub>* in 750 dm*<sup>*3*</sup>* is calculated by the equation:*

  - *moles = *`fraction numerator volume space open parentheses dm cubed close parentheses over denominator 24 end fraction`
- *The mass of SO*<sub>*2*</sub>* is calculated using the equation:*

  - *mass = moles x molar mass, where the molar mass is the relative formula mass in grams*
- *Remember**: This equation calculates the mass in grams but the question asks for it to be in kilograms, so divide your answer by 1000*
- *If you leave your answer to be 2000, you will score 2 marks*

parts.problem_md:
The reaction to produce sulfur trioxide reaches an equilibrium.

2SO<sub>2</sub> (g) + O<sub>2</sub> (g) $\rightleftharpoons$2SO<sub>3</sub> (g)

The forward reaction is exothermic. The rate of attainment of equilibrium and the equilibrium yield of sulfur trioxide are affected by pressure and temperature.

A manufacturer considered two sets of conditions, A and B, for this reaction.

In each case sulfur dioxide is mixed with excess oxygen.

The manufacturer changed the temperature and the pressure and only used a catalyst in B.

The sets of conditions A and B are shown in Figure 7.

| set of conditions | pressure in atm | temperature in °C | catalyst |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2 | 680 | no catalyst used |
| B | 4 | 425 | catalyst used |

**Figure 7**

The manufacturer chooses set of conditions B rather than set of conditions A.

Explain, by considering the effect of changing the conditions on the rate of attainment of equilibrium and on the equilibrium yield of sulfur trioxide, why the manufacturer chooses the set of conditions B rather than the set of conditions A.
parts.solution_md:
The manufacturer chooses the set of conditions B rather than the set of conditions A because:

Chemical ideas expressed:

**Temperature**:

- The equilibrium is reached faster because of the higher temperature in set A 
**OR **
The equilibrium is reached slower because of the lower temperature in set B
- The higher temperature means that there are more frequent collisions because molecules have more energy in set A 
**OR **
The lower temperature means that there are less frequent collisions because molecules have less energy in set B
- The decrease in temperature increases the equilibrium yield but the system takes longer to reach equilibrium
- The temperature chosen for optimum conditions
- The yield lowers / decreases as the forward reaction is exothermic
- A high temperature favours the backwards reaction, which is endothermic
- The equilibrium is reached faster because of the higher pressure in set B 
**OR **
The equilibrium is reached slower because of the lower pressure in set A

**Pressure:**

- Higher pressure causes molecules to be closer together so there are more frequent collisions in set B 
**OR **
Lower pressure causes molecules to be further apart so there are less frequent collisions in set A
- The yield is higher because the products occupy a smaller volume than reactants for set B

**Catalyst:**

- The catalyst used in set B causes the equilibrium to be reached faster
- A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and backward reactions
- The equilibrium position is not affected so the catalyst does not affect the yield

**Level 1:** **(1−2 marks)**

- A basic answer with some chemical ideas, missing information, using simple language and not presented in a logical order

**Level 2:**** ****(3−4 marks)**

- A relevant answer with confidently expressed chemical ideas, a few details missing and some chemical terms included

**Level 3:** **(5−6 marks)**

- A well developed answer that covers chemical ideas in a detailed and logical way, using a wide range of chemical terms

**[Total: 6 marks]**

> * Level 1 answer could be:*

- *A simple explanation of why B was chosen in terms of 2 conditions*
- *A detailed explanation of why B was chosen in terms of 1 condition but may lack a full explanation*

> *An example of a Level 1 answer scoring 2 marks would be:*

> *A lower temperature is used as the forward reaction is exothermic.  A catalyst speeds up the rate of the reaction.*

- *A simple explanation of why B was chosen in terms of temperature and use of a catalyst (2)*

> *Level 2 answer could be:*

- *A simple explanation of why B was chosen in terms of 3 conditions*
- *A simple explanation of why B was chosen in terms of 1 condition **AND **a detailed explanation in terms of 1 other condition*

> *An example of a Level 2 answer scoring 4 marks would be:*

> *Higher pressure is favoured because the rate of reaction is quicker. A catalyst would not affect the yield but it speeds up the time taken to reach equilibrium as it increases the rate of both the forward and reverse reaction, so it reduces the need for higher temperatures.*

- *A simple explanation of why B was chosen in terms of pressure and** **a detailed explanation in terms of the use of a catalyst (4)*

> *Level 3 answer could be:*

- *A detailed explanation of why B was chosen in terms of 2 or more conditions*

> *An example of a Level 3 answer scoring 6 marks would be:*

> *A lower temperature gives a higher yield because the forward reaction is exothermic, so decreasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium position to the right.*

> *A higher pressure gives a higher yield because there are fewer gas molecules on the product side, so increasing pressure favours the forward reaction.*

> *Although a lower temperature would reduce the rate of reaction, a catalyst is used to speed up the rate and allow equilibrium to be reached more quickly.*

> *So condition B is chosen because it increases both the yield (by favouring the forward reaction) and the rate (due to the catalyst and higher pressure).*

- *A detailed explanation of why B was chosen in terms of temperature and pressure and a simple explanation in terms of a catalyst (6)*

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a test tube containing ammonium chloride that has been heated gently.

![thermal-decomposition-of-ammonium-chloride](assets/003-thermal-decomposition-of-ammonium-chloride.png)

Which two gases are present at position Y?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- When the ammonium chloride is heated it decomposes to form ammonia and hydrogen chloride:

NH<sub>4</sub>Cl (s) → NH<sub>3 </sub>(g) + HCl (g)

- As the gases cool down they recombine to form ammonium chloride
- A reversible reaction occurs:

NH<sub>4</sub>Cl (s) ⇌ NH<sub>3 </sub>(g) + HCl (g)

parts.problem_md:
Ammonia is manufactured on a large scale and is used to make fertilisers such as ammonium nitrate (NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub>).

The first stage in the manufacture of ammonium nitrate is to react ammonia gas with oxygen gas.

4NH<sub>3</sub> (g) + 5O<sub>2</sub> (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 4NO (g) + 6H<sub>2</sub>O (g)    Δ*H* = −907 kJ/mol

The reaction is carried out at a pressure of about 10 atm and at a temperature of 800 °C, in the presence of a catalyst.

If the mixture is left for long enough in a sealed container, the reaction reaches a position of dynamic equilibrium.

Graph A shows how the percentage of nitrogen monoxide (NO) in the equilibrium mixture varies with temperature at constant pressure.

Graph B shows how the percentage of nitrogen monoxide (NO) in the equilibrium mixture varies with pressure at a constant temperature.

![screen-shot-2022-10-12-at-20-31-25](assets/004-screen-shot-2022-10-12-at-20-31-25.png)

i) Explain why the percentage of NO at equilibrium decreases in each case.

Graph A:

Graph B:

(4)

ii) Explain why the use of a catalyst has no effect on the position of equilibrium in a reversible reaction.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) The percentage of NO at equilibrium decreases in each case because:

**Graph A:**

An explanation that links the following two points:

*Ignore any references to or arguments based on Le Chatelier’s principle*

- The backward/reverse reaction is endothermic; **[1 mark]**
- So an increase in temperature shifts the equilibrium to the left (hence the percentage of NO decreases); **[1 mark]** 
*Accept the (forward) reaction is exothermic*

**Graph B:**

An explanation that links the following two points:

- There are fewer molecules / moles of gas on the left; **[1 mark]**
- So an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium to the left (hence the percentage of NO decreases);** [1 mark] **

ii) The use of a catalyst has no effect on the position of equilibrium in a reversible reaction.

- (The catalyst/ it) increases the rate of both the forward and reverse reactions; **[1 mark] **
- To the same extent; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 6 marks] **

- *The forward reaction is exothermic, the negative Δ**H**  value tells you this- therefore an increase in temperature will favour the backward reaction and reduce the yield of NO*

  - *4NH*<sub>*3*</sub>* (g) + 5O*<sub>*2*</sub>* (g) *$\rightleftharpoons$* 4NO (g) + 6H*<sub>*2*</sub>*O (g) Δ**H** = −907 kJ/mol*
- *An increase in pressure will favour the side of the reaction with the fewest molecules*

  - *In this case it is the left-hand side *

parts.problem_md:
The second stage in the manufacture of ammonium nitrate is to convert the nitrogen monoxide into nitric acid. The nitric acid is then reacted with concentrated aqueous ammonia as shown in this equation.

HNO<sub>3</sub> (aq) + NH<sub>3</sub> (aq) → NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub> (aq)

i) State, in terms of proton transfer, why this reaction is classified as an acid-base reaction.

(1)

ii) Calculate the volume of 14.8 mol/dm<sup>3</sup> aqueous ammonia that is required to exactly neutralise 150 dm<sup>3</sup> of a solution of nitric acid of concentration 15.8 mol/dm<sup>3</sup>.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) This reaction is classified as an acid-base reaction

- Because a proton is transferred from HNO<sub>3</sub> to NH<sub>3</sub>; **[1 mark] **

ii) The volume of 14.8 mol/dm<sup>3</sup> aqueous ammonia that is required to exactly neutralise 150 dm<sup>3</sup> of a solution of nitric acid of concentration 15.8 mol/dm<sup>3</sup> is:

- Calculate the amount of nitric acid; **[1 mark]**
- Calculate the volume of aqueous ammonia; **[1 mark]**

Example calculation:

n(HNO<sub>3</sub>) = 15.8 × 150 (= 2370 mol)

vol(NH<sub>3</sub>) required = (2370 ÷ 14.8) = 160 (dm<sup>3</sup>)

**[Total: 3 mark] **

- *Remember:** acids donate protons and bases accept protons *
- *In this calculation the values given are slightly higher than you may have seen before - don't be put off, use the same method *

  - *mols = concentration x vol (dm*<sup>*3*</sup>*) Then*
  - *volume (dm*<sup>*3*</sup>*) *<sup>*=*</sup>* *$\frac{\mathrm{mols}}{\mathrm{concentration}}$

parts.problem_md:
Dinitrogen tetraoxide, N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>, is a colourless gas.

Nitrogen dioxide, NO<sub>2</sub>, is a brown gas.

The two gases can exist together in dynamic equilibrium according to the equation:

N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>(g)    $\rightleftharpoons$     2NO<sub>2</sub>(g)

Explain what is meant by the term dynamic equilibrium.
parts.solution_md:
What is meant by the term dynamic equilibrium:

- The reaction is taking place in both directions (at same time); **[1 mark]**
- At an equal rate; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
Some N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> and some NO<sub>2</sub> are put into a sealed gas syringe and allowed to form an equilibrium mixture.

![2c-q71](assets/005-2c-q71.png)

This equilibrium mixture is brown.

i) The pressure of the gas in the syringe is increased by pushing in the piston. The mixture is then allowed to reach a new equilibrium at the same temperature as before.

Explain why the new equilibrium mixture contains less NO<sub>2</sub> than the original equilibrium mixture.

(2)

ii) A student suggests that the new equilibrium mixture would be lighter in colour than the original equilibrium mixture, as there is now less NO<sub>2</sub> present.

Suggest why the new equilibrium mixture is actually darker than the original.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i)  Why the new equilibrium mixture contains less NO<sub>2</sub> than the original equilibrium mixture:

- The position of equilibrium has moved to the left; **[1 mark]**
- As there are fewer moles / molecules (of gas) on the left; **[1 mark]**

ii)  Why the new equilibrium mixture is actually darker than the original:

- The mixture is darker because the concentration of NO<sub>2 </sub>has increased; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *This question is all about using your knowledge  of Le Chatelier's principle to predict what happens when you change the conditions of an equilibrium*
- *You need to use the equation in part a) to figure out how the equilibrium responds*
- *Increasing the pressure causes the equilibrium to shift in the direction that reduces the pressure, in other words the side with fewer gas molecules*
- *It's ok to use words like backwards or towards the reactants, instead of saying left side*
- *Mentioning Le Chatelier's Principle doesn't itself score any credit as it is not asked for in the question and does not appear in the specification, but you need to know how it works*
- *When you increase the pressure it increases the concentration of all the gases present, so although the proportion of NO*<sub>*2*</sub>* in the mixture may have decreased, the molecules of the remaining NO*<sub>*2*</sub>* are closer together in a smaller volume; they are brown in colour so the mixture becomes darker, rather than lighter*

parts.problem_md:
Carbon monoxide, CO, and oxides of nitrogen are produced in a car engine when petrol is burned.

These oxides can be partly removed by using a catalytic converter fitted to the car’s exhaust system.

i)State how oxides of nitrogen are produced in the car engine.

(1)

ii) Give a disadvantage of allowing oxides of nitrogen to escape into the atmosphere.

(1)

iii) Write a chemical equation for the reaction between nitrogen monoxide, NO, and carbon monoxide to form carbon dioxide and nitrogen.

(1)
parts.solution_md:
i)   How oxides of nitrogen are produced in the car engine:

- The nitrogen/N<sub>2</sub> reacts with oxygen/O<sub>2</sub> (both from the air); **[1 mark]**

ii)  A disadvantage of allowing oxides of nitrogen to escape into the atmosphere:

- They form acid rain;** [1 mark]**

iii)   An equation for the reaction between nitrogen monoxide, NO, and carbon monoxide to form carbon dioxide and nitrogen:

- 2NO + 2CO →  N<sub>2 </sub>+ 2CO<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *It part i) it is not right to use the terms combustion or burning as it misses the point of the question which is getting you to show you know it is a side reaction in the engine, rather than something resulting form the combustion of the fuel*
- *For the disadvantage you can get credit by giving specific references to respiratory problems or another harmful effect of acid rain*
- *The nitrogen oxides could contribute to climate change or global warming as they are also greenhouse gases*
- *You can use multiples of fractions in the equation as long as it is balanced*

parts.problem_md:
Hydrogen gas can be produced by reacting a mixture of methane and steam in the presence of a nickel catalyst.

The reaction conditions are a temperature of 700°C and a pressure of 5 atmospheres.

The equation for the reaction is

CH<sub>4 </sub>(g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ CO (g) + 3H<sub>2 </sub>(g)                 Δ*H* = +206 kJ/mol

What does the symbol $\rightleftharpoons$ represent?
parts.solution_md:
The symbol $\rightleftharpoons$ represents a:

- Reversible reaction; **[1 mark]** *Ignore references to equilibrium* 
*Allow the reaction goes both ways* 
*Allow the reaction can go forwards and backwards*

**[Total: 1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
i) The mixture of methane and steam is heated to a temperature greater than 700 °C but the pressure is kept at 5 atmospheres.

Predict the effect of this change on the yield of hydrogen at equilibrium, giving a reason for your answer.

(2)

ii) The mixture of methane and steam is kept at the same temperature of 700 °C but the pressure is increased to more than 5 atmospheres.

Predict the effect of this change on the yield of hydrogen at equilibrium, giving a reason for your answer.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) When the temperature is increased:

- The yield (of hydrogen) increases / more hydrogen is produced;** [1 mark]**
- (Equilibrium shifts to the right as the forward) reaction is endothermic;** [1 mark]** 
*Ignore references to Le Chatelier e.g. an increase in temperature favours the forward reaction*

ii) When the pressure increases:

- The yield (of hydrogen) decreases / less hydrogen is produced;** [1 mark]**
- (Equilibrium shifts to the left as) fewer moles / molecules / particles (of gas) on LHS / more moles / molecules / particles (of gas) on RHS or words to that effect;** [1 mark]** 
*Do not allow atoms* 
*Ignore references to Le Chatelier e.g. an increase in pressure favours the side with fewer moles*

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *Make sure you state what happens to the yield of hydrogen as sometimes students focus on stating what happens to the position of equilibrium but forget to mention about the yield*
- *When explaining changes in the position of equilibrium due to temperature, you should always identify the forward or reverse reaction as exothermic or endothermic*
- *When explaining changes in the position of equilibrium due to pressure, you should always identify which side has the most moles of gas*

parts.problem_md:
Calculate the volume, in dm<sup>3</sup>, of hydrogen gas at rtp that is produced when 10 tonnes of methane gas completely react with steam.

[molar volume of hydrogen at rtp is 24 dm<sup>3</sup>]

Give your answer in standard form.
parts.solution_md:
The volume, in dm<sup>3</sup>, of hydrogen gas at rtp that is produced when 10 tonnes of methane gas completely react with steam is:

- Calculate the amount, in moles, of methane: $\frac{\mathrm{mass}}{\mathrm{molar} \mathrm{mass}}=\frac{10,000,000}{16}$ **OR **625,000; **[1 mark]**
- Use the equation to calculate the amount of hydrogen: 625,000 x 3 **OR** 1,875,000; **[1 mark]**
- Multiply amount by 24 to find the volume of hydrogen: 1,875,000 x 24 **OR** 45,000,000 (dm<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]**
- Final answer in standard form: 4.5 x 10<sup>7</sup> (dm<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]** *45,000,000 without working scores 3 marks* *4.5 x 10*<sup>*7 *</sup>*without working scores 4 marks*

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *It is very important to write down your working clearly, as you can still pick up marks, even if you get the final answer wrong*
- *Note**: The answer is required to be in standard form, even if you get your working wrong, you can still gain this final mark for correctly converting an incorrect answer to standard form*
- *Common answers are:*

  - *4.5 x 10*<sup>*4*</sup>* (3 marks)*
  - *45,000 (2 marks)*
  - *4.5 x 10*<sup>*1*</sup>* (3 marks)*
  - *45 (2 marks)*
  - *1.5 x 10*<sup>*7*</sup>* (3 marks)*
  - *15,000,000 (2 marks)*

parts.problem_md:
The decomposition of ammonium chloride is endothermic:

**NH**<sub>**4**</sub>**Cl (s) **$\rightleftharpoons$**NH**<sub>**3**</sub>** (g) + HCl (g)**

Which changes to the conditions would both decrease the amount of product in this reaction?

|   | ** ** | **Change 1** | **Change 2** |
|---|---|---|---|
| ☐ | **A** | Increase pressure | Decrease temperature |
| ☐ | **B** | Decrease pressure | Decrease temperature |
| ☐ | **C** | Increase pressure | Increase temperature |
| ☐ | **D** | Decrease pressure | Increase temperature |
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- An increase in pressure causes the equilibrium position to shift towards the side with the smaller number of molecules of gas, as shown by the symbol equation for that reaction, which is the reactant side in the reaction

  - This means that the relative amount of product decreases
- A decrease in temperature for an endothermic reaction causes the equilibrium position to shift to decrease the relative amount of products

parts.problem_md:
Hydrated copper sulfate is a blue salt that contains water molecules within its lattice structure. When heated, the water is removed from the structure, forming white anhydrous copper sulfate.

Complete the word equation for the reaction.

hydrated copper sulfate   $\rightleftharpoons$   ____________________   +   ____________________
parts.solution_md:
The missing products are:

- Anhydrous copper sulfate; **[1 mark]**
- Water; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *The correct equation is:*

  - *hydrated copper sulfate  *$\rightleftharpoons$*  anhydrous copper sulfate   +   water*
- *The information required is given in the question and the words can be in either order*

parts.problem_md:
A student heated hydrated copper sulfate using the equipment in **Figure 1**.

**Figure 1**

![aqa-gcse-6-2e-tq2b-hydrated-copper-sulfate](assets/006-aqa-gcse-6-2e-tq2b-hydrated-copper-sulfate.png)

What **two **observations would be made when hydrated copper sulfate was heated?

Tick (✓) **two **boxes.

| Hydrated copper sulfate turns white |   |
|---|---|
| Hydrated copper sulfate turns blue |   |
| Substance **A** is a colourless liquid |   |
| Substance **A** is a white solid |   |
| Substance **A** is a blue solution |   |
parts.solution_md:
The two observations would be:

| Hydrated copper sulfate turns white | ✓; **[1 mark]** |
|---|---|
| Hydrated copper sulfate turns blue |   |
| Substance **A** is a colourless liquid | ✓; **[1 mark]** |
| Substance **A** is a white solid |   |
| Substance **A** is a blue solution |   |

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *When blue hydrated copper sulfate is heated, anhydrous copper sulfate and water are produced*
- *Anhydrous copper sulfate is white*
- *The water that is produced will be a gas (steam) which will travel down the delivery tube into the empty test tube*
- *The ice around the empty test tube cools the steam which condenses to form water (a colourless liquid)*

parts.problem_md: When hydrated copper sulfate is heated, an endothermic reaction occurs. What type of reaction occurs when water is added to anhydrous copper sulfate?
parts.solution_md:
When water is added to anhydrous copper sulfate, the reaction is :

- Exothermic; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *Water added to anhydrous copper sulfate is the reverse reaction of hydrated copper sulfate being heated*
- *If a reversible reaction is endothermic in one direction, it will be exothermic in the opposite direction*

parts.problem_md: 5.2 g of hydrated copper sulfate was heated in a test tube.  3.0 g of anhydrous copper sulfate remained after heating. Calculate the mass of water that was given off in grams**.**
parts.solution_md:
The mass of water given off is:

- 5.2 - 3.0; **[1 mark]**
- = 2.2 (g); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *The mass of the reactant (hydrated copper sulfate) will be equal to the mass of the products (anhydrous copper sulfate and water)*
- *The mass of the water will therefore be the mass of hydrated copper sulfate - the mass of anhydrous copper sulfate*
- *You can score 2 marks for a correct answer with no working*

parts.problem_md:
Ammonia can be made from nitrogen and hydrogen during the Haber process.  The forward reaction is exothermic.

N<sub>2</sub>   +   3H<sub>2</sub>    $\rightleftharpoons$      2NH<sub>3</sub>

What does the$\rightleftharpoons$ symbol mean?
parts.solution_md:
The $\rightleftharpoons$symbol means:

- The reaction is reversible; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *A reversible reaction is one which goes in both directions*

  - *The nitrogen and hydrogen react to form ammonia*
  - *The ammonia can reform the hydrogen and nitrogen*

parts.problem_md: The Haber process is exothermic.  What is meant by an **exothermic reaction**?
parts.solution_md:
An **exothermic reaction **is:

- (One that) releases (heat) energy to the surroundings 
**AND** 
The temperature increases; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *You will not score the mark for stating either point, both must be made*
- *Remember:** **EX**othermic reactions = energy **EX**its *

parts.problem_md:
#### Separate: Chemistry Only Use words from the box to complete the sentences to explain the effect of increasing pressure on the yield of ammonia. | \| increase \| decrease \| forward \|
\|---\|---\|---\|

\| fewer \| reverse \| more \| \|
\|---\|---\|---\|---\| | |---| Increasing pressure will cause the rate of the ________ reaction to increase. This is because there are _______ molecules on the right hand side which will reduce the pressure. The yield of ammonia will __________.
parts.solution_md:
The completed sentences are:

- Increasing pressure will cause the rate of the **forward** reaction to increase; ** [1 mark]**
- This is because there are **fewer** molecules on the right hand side which will reduce the pressure; ** [1 mark]**
- The yield of ammonia will **increase**;** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *Any change made to the system, the system will try and oppose the change*
- *Increasing pressure will result in the position of equilibrium shifting to decrease it again *
- *To reduce pressure, the reaction that produces fewer molecules of gas is always favoured, in this case, the forward reaction *
- *If the forward reaction occurs at a higher rate than the reverse reaction, more ammonia will be produced*

parts.problem_md: Give one factor which will not** **affect the position of equilibrium for the reaction in part a).
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- A catalyst only changes the rate at which the equilibrium is reached, not the position of it
- Using a catalyst, speeds up the rate of reaction
- Increasing temperature causes the equilibrium to favour the endothermic reaction, the reverse reaction
- Increasing the concentration of hydrogen will result in the system trying to reduce the concentration of hydrogen and favour the forward reaction

parts.problem_md:
This question is about equilibrium.

An ionic equation for the reaction between iron (III), Fe<sup>3+</sup> and thiocyanate ions, SCN<sup>2+</sup> is shown below:

At room temperature, the mixture of the equilibrium solution is orange.

|   | Fe<sup>3+</sup> (aq)      + | SCN<sup>-</sup> (aq)       ⇌ | FeSCN<sup>2+ </sup>(aq) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colour of solution | yellow | colourless | red |

Which solvent would be used to dissolve the ions in this reaction?
parts.solution_md:
The solvent used to dissolve the ions is:

- Water; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 1 mark]**

- *The equation shows the (aq) state symbol which indicates the ions are dissolved in water*

parts.problem_md: Explain the effect, if any, of changing pressure on the colour of the equilibrium mixture.
parts.solution_md:
The effect of pressure will be:

- No effect on the change of colour; **[1 mark]**
- The position of equilibrium does not change; **[1 mark]**
- (Because) there are no gases present 
**OR** 
There are only ions in aqueous solutions present; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *Remember:** pressure will only affect reactions that involve gases so look carefully at the equation *
- *Look at the number of marks to help you*

  - *What is the effect on the colour? There is no effect on the colour*
  - *Why is there no effect? Because the position of the equilibrium doesn't change*
  - *Why does the position of equilibrium not change? Because the reaction does not involve gases*
- *This question is usually asked for a reaction involving gases when the number of molecules of product and reactant is the same so make sure you double check the state symbols*

parts.problem_md:
A few drops of a colourless solution containing a high concentration of Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions are added to the orange equilibrium mixture.

Explain the colour change observed.
parts.solution_md:
The colour change observed is:

- The mixture becomes (more) red; **[1 mark]**
- (Because) the position of) equilibrium moves to the right 
**OR** 
(Because) the concentration of Fe<sup>3+</sup> increases 
**OR** 
(Because) the forward reaction is favoured; **[1 mark]**
- (So that) the concentration of Fe<sup>3+</sup> is reduced / so that the increase in Fe<sup>3+</sup> is counteracted;** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *Remember: **When a condition is changed (temperature, pressure, concentration), the system will oppose the change made*
- *So if the concentration of Fe*<sup>*3+ *</sup>*is increased then the system will try and reduce the concentration*
- *In order to do this, the rate of the forward reaction will increase and more  FeSCN*<sup>*2+ *</sup>*will be produced which is red*

parts.problem_md:
A water bath is set up at a temperature below room temperature.

When a test tube containing the orange equilibrium mixture is placed in the water bath, the mixture becomes more red.

Explain what this shows about the energy change for the forward reaction.
parts.solution_md:
The forward reaction is:

- Exothermic 
**OR** 
The forward reaction releases energy;** [1 mark]**
- (Because) the equilibrium moves to the right 
**OR** 
The forward reaction is favoured; **[1 mark]**
- So that the reduction in temperature is increased 
**OR** 
So that the reduction in temperature is counteracted; **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *If the solution is placed in a water bath below room temperature, the temperature of the reaction has been decreased*
- *The reaction will oppose this change and attempt to increase the temperature *
- *A red solution is observed*

  - *The forward reaction produces a red solution so the rate of the forward reaction must have increased *
- *The forward reaction must therefore be exothermic *

parts.problem_md:
The Haber process is an example of a reversible reaction where the forward reaction is exothermic:

N<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub> (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NH<sub>3</sub> (g)

What is** **not true about this system when it is at equilibrium?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- When a system is at equilibrium

  - The energy change of the reverse reaction is the opposite of the energy change of the forward reaction
  - The equilibrium exists in a closed system
  - The forward and reverse reactions continue to occur but at equal rates, with no overall change in the concentrations of reactants or products

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: The energy change of the reverse reaction is endothermic

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: The equilibrium occurs within a closed system

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: The reaction has reached completion and stopped

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: The rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction

parts.problem_md:
This question is about ammonia gas, NH<sub>3</sub>

Ammonia can be prepared in a laboratory from the reaction between ammonium chloride, NH<sub>4</sub>Cl, and sodium hydroxide. The other products of the reaction are sodium chloride and water.

i) Give a chemical equation for this reaction.

(1)

ii) Give a test for ammonia gas.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) The equation is:

- NH<sub>4</sub>Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH<sub>3</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O;** [1 mark] **

ii) The test for ammonium gas

- Moist/damp red litmus paper; **[1 mark] **
- Turns blue; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 3 marks]**** **

- *You can also use universal indicator paper as it will also turn blue *
- *Either way, the paper must be damp as the gas needs something to dissolve into*

parts.problem_md:
In industry, ammonia is produced from nitrogen and hydrogen. The equation for this reaction is

N<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub> (g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NH<sub>3</sub> (g)

In a sealed container, the reaction can reach a position of **dynamic equilibrium**. Explain the meaning of the term dynamic equilibrium.
parts.solution_md:
The meaning of the term dynamic equilibrium:

An explanation linking following two points:

- Forward and backward / reverse reactions are taking place at same rate; **[1 mark]**
- The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 2 marks]**** **

- *You can also gain the mark for saying reaction is taking place in both directions at same rate*
- *However you will not gain a mark for saying concentrations of the reactants and products are equal / the same*

  - *The concentrations of products and reactants remain constant, it does not mean that they are equal to one another*

parts.problem_md:
The graph shows the percentage yield of ammonia at equilibrium for different temperatures and pressures.

![screen-shot-2022-10-19-at-20-56-02](assets/007-screen-shot-2022-10-19-at-20-56-02.png)

Using the graph, explain if the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
parts.solution_md:
The forward reaction is:

An explanation linking following two points:

- As temperature decreases yield of ammonia (formed in forward reaction) increases; **[1 mark] **
- So forward reaction is exothermic; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 2 marks]**** **

- *You will gain the mark for saying as temperature decreases equilibrium position shifts in forward direction / (from left) to right (producing more ammonia)*
- *This question is very specific as you must state that the reaction is exothermic or endothermic *

  - *The graph shows that the higher temperature the lower the yield of ammonia*
  - *Therefore the forward reaction must be exothermic *
  - *Le Chatelier’s Principle states that when a change is made to the conditions of a system at equilibrium, the system automatically moves to oppose** **the change - this however does not answer the question directly and any references to Le Chatelier’s Principle are not given credit*

parts.problem_md:
This question is about reactions involving gases.

Potassium carbonate reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce carbon dioxide gas.

The equation for the reaction is

K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3 </sub>(s) + 2HCl (aq) → 2KCl (aq) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g)

Calculate the volume, in cm<sup>3</sup>, of carbon dioxide gas produced when 6.9 g of potassium carbonate reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid.

[*M*<sub>*r*</sub> of K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> = 138]

[molar volume of CO<sub>2</sub> at rtp = 24 dm<sup>3</sup>]

volume = .............................................................. cm<sup>3</sup>
parts.solution_md:
To calculate the volume, in cm<sup>3</sup>, of carbon dioxide gas produced

Calculation with following steps

- Calculation of n(K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>); **[1 mark]**
- Deduction of n(CO<sub>2</sub>) and vol (CO<sub>2</sub>) by multiplying by 24 (dm<sup>3</sup>); **[1 mark]**
- Correct evaluation of volume in cm<sup>3</sup>; **[1 mark] **

Example calculation

n(K<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) = 6.9 ÷ 138 = 0.05

vol(CO<sub>2</sub>) = 0.05 x 24 (dm<sup>3</sup>)

vol(CO<sub>2</sub>) = 1200 (cm<sup>3</sup>)

**[Total: 3 marks] **

- *For this question you need to use two equations:*
- *Moles = *$\frac{Mass}{M_{r}}$* and Volume of a gas in cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* = moles x 24 000*
- *If asked for the volume in dm*<sup>*3*</sup>* you would multiply by 24*
- *Note that the equation gives a 1:1 ratio of K*<sub>*2*</sub>*CO*<sub>*3*</sub>* to CO*<sub>*2*</sub>*, so there is no need to multiply or divide the number of moles calculated *

parts.problem_md:
This reaction involving gases is in dynamic equilibrium at a temperature of 225°C.

H<sub>2</sub> (g) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g) → CO (g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (g) Δ*H* = + 41 kJ/mol

i) Predict the effect on the yield of CO (g) at equilibrium when the temperature is increased without changing the pressure.

Give a reason for your answer.

(2)

ii) Predict the effect on the yield of CO (g) at equilibrium when the pressure is increased without changing the temperature.

Give a reason for your answer.

(2)
parts.solution_md:
i) The effect on the yield of CO (g) at equilibrium when the temperature is increased

- Higher yield of CO; **[1 mark] **
- Because (equilibrium shifts to the right as the forward) reaction is endothermic; **[1 mark] **

ii) The effect on the yield of CO (g) at equilibrium when the pressure is increased

- No effect (on yield); **[1 mark] **
- Because equal numbers of moles / molecules (of gas) on both sides; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *You can be awarded the first mark for part (i) for saying more CO produced but will not be given the mark for referencing references to Le Chatelier’s Principle e.g. increasing temperature favours the forward reaction*

  - *This is because you are not relating it to the given equation *
  - *You need to apply Le Chatelier’s Principle to this equation be given the second mark*

parts.problem_md:
This question is about chemical equilibrium and reversible reactions.

If carried out in a closed system, reversible reactions can reach a state of equilibrium.

Explain what a closed system is.
parts.solution_md:
A closed system means:

- No reactant or product can leave or enter the reaction vessel; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
When a reversible reaction reaches equilibrium, it appears to have stopped.

Explain why.
parts.solution_md:
The reaction appears to have stopped because:

- The forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate; **[1 mark] **
- So there is no overall change in quantities / concentrations of reactants and products; **[1 mark] **

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *Careful: **You cannot say that the quantities / concentrations of the reactants and products are the same*
- *They do not change but they are not the same as each other *

parts.problem_md:
In the Haber process, the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to produce ammonia is reversible.

N<sub>2 </sub>(g)     +     3H<sub>2 </sub>(g)     ⇌      2NH<sub>3 </sub>(g)

Explain what happens to the amount of ammonia produced at equilibrium if the pressure is increased.
parts.solution_md:
When the pressure increases:

- The amount / yield of ammonia increases; **[1 mark] **
- Equilibrium shifts to the right / product side; **[1 mark] **
- Because the right side has fewer moles / molecules of gas; **[1 mark] **
*Allow because there are 2 moles on the RHS and 4 moles on the LHS*
*Reject 'atoms'*

**[Total: 3 marks]**

- *When you see a question regarding the position of equilibrium and pressure, count the number of moles / molecules of each substance*
- *Some students make the mistake of counting the number of atoms, not molecules- the molecules is the big number in front of the formula, if there is no number, there is one molecule of that substance*

parts.problem_md:
Describe the effect, if any, of using a catalyst on:

- the rate of reaction
- the position of equilibrium
parts.solution_md:
The effect of a catalyst on the rate of reaction and position of equilibrium:

- Increases the rate of reaction;** [1 mark]**
- No effect on position of equilibrium; ** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 2 marks]**

- *A catalyst will increase the rate of reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy *
- *It cannot change the position of the equilibrium just help equilibrium be established faster *
